body:
incident-bot: ALERT: 3 alerts firing: canary-pool-canary-v3 p99 > 6s, streaming-stalls > 30/min, sLO-breach:region-us-east. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/canary-v3

Sam - oncall: Ack, paging in. I'm looking at p95/p99 graphs now. Noticing p99 jumped to ~6.4s at 13:04 UTC, p95 around 450ms.

Ava - CS: Customer ZoomFlow reported degraded streaming UX at ~13:05, they saw repeated stalls then reconnects. They're asking if we're rolling back.

Priya - runtime: I rolled a canary of v3 encoder at 12:50 (rush-hour ramp to 20%). Initial metrics looked fine until a tail surge at 13:03. I’m seeing a subtotal of stalled streams pinned to a small set of hosts in the canary pool.

Miguel - SRE: Logs show repeated `KV_CACHE_LOCK` backpressure on those hosts and a handful of `encoder_quant_step` ops taking >> expected time. Dump from host canary-03: ```
2026-03-01T13:03:04Z ERROR encoder_worker: quant_step took 8.3s id=0x7f2a
2026-03-01T13:03:04Z WARN  kv_cache: lock_wait 124ms key=prefix_0xabc
2026-03-01T13:03:05Z INFO  stream: stall detected session=zz-123
```

Sam - oncall: Are stalls showing up as stream-level timeouts or are they token-level hung RTs?

Priya - runtime: Token-level generation is hanging — not network timeouts. The request enters the runtime, the kv cache call to restore context blocks sometimes and cascades into the attention kernel. It's concentrated on the canary hosts.

Miguel - SRE: I'm running a targeted `strace` + perf on canary-03 thread pool. Also checking kernel CPU steal and NVLink errors. So far no hardware errors. Could be a regression in the encoder's cache handling under concurrent sess loads.

Sam - oncall: Impact: multiple hosted customers routed to canary are affected; overall p99 for the zone is above our SLO. Paging owner for rollout decisions. @deploy-bot can you check the rollout state and traffic weights?

deploy-bot: rollout status: canary-v3 -> target=20% currently active. Hosts healthy=3/5 (2 flaky). Recent deploy at 12:50. Can perform rollback or reduce traffic.

Priya - runtime: Recommend immediate traffic reduction to 5% for canary and freeze further ramps. If stalls persist reduce to 0% and abort rollout. Reducing traffic is fast and less disruptive than full rollback.

Sam - oncall: Agreed. Doing an emergency traffic shift now. Command: ```
redwood rollout adjust --name canary-v3 --weight 5
```

Sam - oncall: Executed. Confirming new routing: canary weight=5%. Observed drop in new sessions to canary hosts within 30s.

Ava - CS: ZoomFlow says they're still seeing occasional stalls but overall improvement. They appreciate the quick action. :thumbsup:

Miguel - SRE: While traffic dropped, tail latency remains elevated on the two flaky hosts. I'm starting a controlled drain of those instances and will isolate them from the LB. Can someone confirm we can cordon canary-03 and canary-04?

Priya - runtime: Cordon is fine. Doing `kubectl cordon canary-03` and `drain` sequence now. Expect ongoing in-flight streams to be retried to fallback.

deploy-bot: cordon initiated for canary-03. drain status: in-flight streams 12 -> 0 in 45s. Host cordoned.

Sam - oncall: After cordon, p99 dropped to ~2.1s in the canary slice and overall region p99 to 1.2s. Still above ideal but within error budget for today.

Priya - runtime: Given the persistent kernel-level delay patterns, I propose aborting the canary (set weight 0) and rolling back to v2 encoder for a full validation in a staging-like traffic shape. Any objections?

Miguel - SRE: +1. We'll capture perf traces from the cordoned hosts and attach to the incident. Please do not repro deploy until trace analysis.

Sam - oncall: Proceeding: ```
redwood rollout adjust --name canary-v3 --weight 0
redwood rollout abort --name canary-v3 --reason "tail-quantization-latency during rush-hour"
```

deploy-bot: Rollout aborted. Traffic weight for canary-v3 set to 0. Rollback to v2 encoder initiated on canary pool. rollback job id=rb-20260301-01.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=sev2. Impact: elevated p99 for us-east hosted API for ~13:03-13:18 UTC. Affected customers: ZoomFlow (partial), internal canary tests. Incident assigned to Sam/Miguel for mitigation, Priya for runtime root cause.

Ava - CS: Follow-up: ZoomFlow reported transient user-facing stalls; they want a brief RCA once we have one. I'll open a CS ticket and hold a customer note template.

Priya - runtime: I'll collect the traces and post links. Early guess: a concurrency regression in the encoder's quantization path causing extended holding of kv-cache locks under certain sequence lengths. Not ruling out rare model weights interacting with kernel selection.

Miguel - SRE: Captured perf profile + strace + kernel sched logs. Uploading to: https://artifacts.redwood.example/incident/2061102222/traces.tar.gz

Sam - oncall: Handoff in 30min to next oncall. Leaving action items: 1) Priya & research team to debug quant path, 2) Miguel to scrub hosts for hardware anomalies and preserve VM images, 3) Sam to draft incident timeline and customer note.

Sam - oncall: Next oncall (Miguel) you have the incident. I'll update #incidents with a short summary and mark as mitigated once rollback completes.

Miguel - SRE: Taking it. Will monitor for 2 hours and sync with Priya at 14:30 UTC.

Priya - runtime: Quick question: do we want a temporary automatic safety gate on future canary ramps to pause if p99 > 3s for >1 min? We can add that to the rollout pipeline.

Sam - oncall: Yes please. Create a GH issue and tag rollout automation. Assign to Priya.

Priya - runtime: Filed issue: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/4721 - "canary safety gate: pause on p99 breach during ramp". Assigning to myself.

Ava - CS: I'll keep ZoomFlow updated with a short note: what happened, mitigation done (traffic reduced + rollback), and ETA for RCA.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigation confirmed, rollback completed, severity de-escalated to sev3 for follow-up. Close criteria: RCA + follow-up send to customers.

Sam - oncall: Closing thread for active paging. We'll keep the artifacts and notes in the incident ticket. Postmortem owners: Priya (root cause), Miguel (host analysis), Sam (timeline + customer comms).

Priya - runtime: Adding one more note: prioritize reproducer that simulates rush-hour affload with small sequences + heavy KV cache churn. That will be the main test case.

Miguel - SRE: Copy. I'll snapshot the two cordoned hosts and tag them with `incident-2061102222` for deep-dive.

Ava - CS: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the customer note once Sam posts the timeline.

Sam - oncall: Thanks. Handing off fully to Miguel. /end
